exactDelta.changeSummary: Adds explicit uniform-drift continuum idealization; replaces universal traversal by equality of transported net signed charge to slab charge; explicitly denies traversal by every original particle and distinguishes random motion from average drift transport.

freshAffectedSCI.originalDefect: Mean directed velocity was used to conclude that every particle originally in the segment crossed section 2.
freshAffectedSCI.derivation: For a homogeneous stationary carrier distribution with mean normal drift v > 0, the oriented number flux across area S is n S v. Thus net transported signed charge over dt is q0 n S v dt. At dt = dl/v, this is q0 n S dl, the signed charge assigned to the slab in the continuum model. Equality of those amounts does not identify the transported carriers with every original slab particle. Random forward and backward crossings contribute with opposite orientations; the net is fixed by their mean, not by individual traversal.
freshAffectedSCI.originalCounterexampleRetested: Take uniform equal-density subpopulations with velocities 0 and 2v. The mean is v and their total oriented flux is n S v. At dl/v, stationary original particles still do not cross section 2, although the net transported charge equals q0 n S dl. The corrected text expressly permits this counterexample and no longer asserts its false conclusion.
freshAffectedSCI.additionalCounterexample: Equal-density populations with velocities -3v and 5v also have mean v and net flux n S v. Some original particles move away from section 2 while faster incoming particles contribute from upstream. This again preserves the corrected net-charge equality without requiring every original carrier to traverse.

freshAffectedSCI.modelLimits: The equality is a uniform stationary mean/continuum transport result, not a claim about a finite sample's exact fluctuating microscopic trajectories. The elapsed-time construction uses the expressly rightward v > 0 example.
freshAffectedSCI.disposition: Resolved. The explicit continuum qualification, net-charge formulation and denial of universal original-particle traversal directly address the original finding.
